subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated flag, or fold it into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the trust boundary for elevated host exec across persisted cron jobs, agent-created schedules, heartbeat state, and upgrades, which requires maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Fold into scheduling provenance
options.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design and keep heartbeat provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement narrow elevated markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with explicit migration and tests for create, update, and execution-time checks.

options.title: Remove internal-source elevation
options.body: Fail closed for cron-event and heartbeat elevated access unless maintainers intentionally preserve a separate compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold into scheduling provenance
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design and keep heartbeat provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged cron caller-scope work makes this the closest current owner path for scheduling provenance decisions.
